answer.short_answer:
At baseline, 312 participants were classified as uncontrolled, 0 as controlled, and 1 was missing; at week 8, 72 were uncontrolled, 229 were controlled, and none were missing. [ClinicalTrials.gov:NCT00545844]

The study evaluated the effect of adding montelukast to inhaled corticosteroids in adults with uncontrolled asthma and allergic rhinitis, using a within‑subject pre‑post design rather than a parallel control group. [ClinicalTrials.gov:NCT00545844]

history.question: For NCT00545844, what were the asthma control results at baseline and week 8? Give the counts and denominators, explain which treatment was studied and what the comparison can tell us.
history.answer:
At baseline, 312 participants were classified as uncontrolled, 0 as controlled, and 1 was missing; at week 8, 72 were uncontrolled, 229 were controlled, and none were missing. [ClinicalTrials.gov:NCT00545844]

The study evaluated the effect of adding montelukast to inhaled corticosteroids in adults with uncontrolled asthma and allergic rhinitis, using a within‑subject pre‑post design rather than a parallel control group. [ClinicalTrials.gov:NCT00545844]

evidence.title: A Study to Investigate the Safety, Tolerability and Effects of AZD8630 in Healthy Subjects and Subjects With Asthma on Inhaled Corticosteroids and Long-acting Beta-agonists
evidence.metadata_scope: Stored registry status and phase describe study progress/design, not whether measured results are posted. Protocol wording alone does not establish that a study is still ongoing.
evidence.content_scope: Only protocol brief summary/detailed description were indexed from this fetched record; structured results tables were not indexed. Results may exist elsewhere.
evidence.text: This is a first in human (FIH) clinical study to evaluate the safety, tolerability, pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics of AZD8630 in healthy adults (Part A) and adult asthma patients on medium to high dose inhaled corticosteroids / Long-acting beta-agonists (Part B) The study is divided in 2 parts, A and B. Part A will be conducted in healthy adults, whereas Part B will be conducted in adult asthma patients on medium/high dose inhaled corticosteroids (ICS)/long-acting beta-agonists (LABA) to evaluate the safety, tolerability, pharmacokinetics (PK), and immunogenicity of AZD8630 by dry powder inhaler (DPI) administration. Part A includes the assessment of the PK and safety of intravenous (IV) AZD8630. Part A consists of single ascending dose (SAD) and multiple ascending dose (MAD) cohorts in sequential order and Part B will be evaluating multiple dose levels. Part A: This part will consist 4 sub-parts and will include healthy participants and healthy participants of Chinese and Japanese ethnicity. These participants will randomized to receive AZD8630 and to receive placebo. * Sub-Part A1, SAD in healthy participants (one cohort in Sub-Part A1 will receive IV AZD8630 \[IV formulation\]) * Sub-Part A2, SAD in healthy participants of Chinese and Japanese ethnicity * Sub-Part A3, MAD in healthy participants * Sub-Part A4, MAD in healthy participants of Chinese and Japanese ethnicity Part B: Adult asthma patients will be randomized to one of 3 inhaled dose levels of AZD8630 or placebo. The expected duration of study participation for each participants in the part A is up to 87 days, and each patients in the Part B is up to 70 days.
